Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: All living organisms are made up of cells.
False 1: Most living organisms are made up of cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The cell represents the basic level at which life exists.
False 1: The tissue represents the basic level at which life exists.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Some organisms, such as bacteria or yeast, consist of only one cell (unicellular), while others like plants, fish, birds or humans are made up of millions of cells (multicellular).
False 1: Some organisms, such as bacteria or yeast, consist of only one cell (unicellular), while others like plants, fish, birds or humans are made up of thousands of cells (multicellular).

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: A group of similar cells performing similar functions forms tissues; different tissues are organised to form an organ and several organs work together to form organ systems.
False 1: A group of different cells performing different functions forms tissues.
False 2: A group of similar cells performing similar functions forms organs.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The limit of resolution of the human eye is 0.1 mm when viewed from about 25 cm (the near point of the human eye).
False 1: The limit of resolution of the human eye is 1 mm.
False 2: The limit of resolution of the human eye is 0.01 mm.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Robert Hooke was the first person to observe a cell in 1665 using a self-designed microscope capable of about 200–300X magnification.
False 1: Matthias Schleiden was the first person to observe a cell in 1665.
False 2: Robert Hooke was the first person to observe a cell in 1839.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: While examining a thin slice of cork, Hooke observed small box-like compartments and named them 'cells'.
False 1: While examining a thin slice of onion, Hooke observed small box-like compartments and named them 'cells'.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Electron microscopes use a beam of electrons instead of light to produce highly magnified images, allowing us to see cell structure at the nanometre scale.
False 1: Electron microscopes use a beam of light instead of electrons to produce highly magnified images.
False 2: Light microscopes use a beam of electrons instead of light to produce highly magnified images.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The cell membrane is a thin boundary that surrounds a cell and protects its contents; it defines the individuality of a cell and is also called the plasma membrane.
False 1: The cell wall is a thin boundary that surrounds a cell and protects its contents; it defines the individuality of a cell and is also called the plasma membrane.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, which means it allows some substances to pass through it while blocking others.
False 1: The cell wall is selectively permeable, which means it allows some substances to pass through it while blocking others.
False 2: The cell membrane is freely permeable, which means it allows all substances to pass through it.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The cell membrane is about 7 to 10 nanometres (nm) thick and is made up of lipids (fats) and proteins.
False 1: The cell membrane is about 70 to 100 nanometres (nm) thick.
False 2: The cell membrane is made up of carbohydrates and nucleic acids.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution (more water, less solute) to a concentrated solution (less water, more solute).
False 1: Osmosis is the movement of solute through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution.
False 2: Diffusion is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration, and it occurs even without a membrane.
False 1: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a lower to a higher concentration.
False 2: Osmosis is the net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration and occurs even without a membrane.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In plants, water from the soil enters root cells by the process of osmosis.
False 1: In plants, water from the soil enters root cells by the process of diffusion.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The fluid-mosaic model describes a cell membrane with a lipid bilayer — water-attracting heads facing outwards and water-repelling tails facing inwards — with proteins embedded in them.
False 1: The fluid-mosaic model describes a lipid bilayer with water-attracting heads facing inwards and water-repelling tails facing outwards.
False 2: The fluid-mosaic model describes a protein bilayer with lipid molecules embedded in them.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The molecules in the cell membrane can move sideways, flip and rotate within the membrane (making it 'fluid'); since the molecules are arranged like tiles in a mosaic, it is called the 'mosaic' model.
False 1: The molecules in the cell membrane are fixed in place and cannot move, making it rigid; it is still called the 'mosaic' model.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Plant cells have an additional covering outside the cell membrane called a cell wall, which helps leaves and flowers remain firm and maintains their shapes.
False 1: Animal cells have an additional covering outside the cell membrane called a cell wall.
False 2: Plant cells have an additional covering outside the cell membrane called a nuclear envelope.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Although rigid, the cell wall is permeable — water and some dissolved minerals can pass through it.
False 1: Although rigid, the cell wall is selectively permeable — only certain molecules can pass through it, blocking water.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: When a plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution, it loses water through osmosis; the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall, but the rigid cell wall maintains the cell's shape.
False 1: When a plant cell is placed in a dilute solution, it loses water through osmosis and the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Animal cells do not have a cell wall; therefore, when placed in a concentrated sugar solution, they lose water and shrink.
False 1: Plant cells do not have a cell wall; therefore, when placed in a concentrated sugar solution, they lose water and shrink.
False 2: Animal cells do not have a cell wall; therefore, when placed in a dilute solution, they lose water and shrink.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The plant cell wall is primarily made of cellulose, a type of carbohydrate formed by many glucose units linked together.
False 1: The plant cell wall is primarily made of chitin, a type of carbohydrate.
False 2: The plant cell wall is primarily made of proteins formed by many amino acid units linked together.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Cellulose in our diet acts as roughage, helping in digestion.
False 1: Cellulose in our diet acts as a primary energy source, providing caloric nutrition.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Some microorganisms, like fungi and bacteria, also have a cell wall to provide protection and structural support to their cells.
False 1: All animals also have a cell wall to provide protection and structural support to their cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Most cells have three basic parts: a selectively permeable plasma membrane, a semi-fluid jelly-like substance called the cytoplasm, and a prominent nucleus.
False 1: Most cells have two basic parts: a plasma membrane and a nucleus, with no cytoplasm.
False 2: The cytoplasm is a rigid, solid substance found inside the cell.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The cytoplasm contains several sub-cellular components called organelles, along with other substances, most of which are only visible with an electron microscope.
False 1: The nucleus contains several sub-cellular components called organelles, along with other substances.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: A bacterial cell lacks a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; such cells are called prokaryotic cells (pro means primitive, karyon means nucleus).
False 1: A plant cell lacks a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; such cells are called prokaryotic cells.
False 2: A bacterial cell has a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; such cells are called prokaryotic cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In prokaryotic cells, most cellular activities take place directly in the cytoplasm.
False 1: In eukaryotic cells, most cellular activities take place directly in the cytoplasm without membrane-bound organelles.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Plant and animal cells have a well-defined nucleus and several membrane-bound organelles and are called eukaryotic cells (eu means true, karyon means nucleus).
False 1: Bacterial cells have a well-defined nucleus and several membrane-bound organelles and are called eukaryotic cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The typical diameter of a prokaryotic cell is 1 to 10 µm; prokaryotic organisms are usually unicellular.
False 1: The typical diameter of a prokaryotic cell is 10 to 100 µm.
False 2: Prokaryotic organisms can be unicellular or multicellular.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Eukaryotic cells have a typical diameter of 10 to 100 µm and can be unicellular or multicellular.
False 1: Eukaryotic cells have a typical diameter of 1 to 10 µm.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The nucleus has a double-layered covering called the nuclear membrane, which has pores that allow the transfer of material between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
False 1: The nucleus has a single-layered covering called the nuclear membrane.
False 2: The cell membrane has pores that allow the transfer of material between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The nucleolus is the dense round body in the nucleus, where synthesis of ribosomal subunits takes place.
False 1: The nucleolus is the dense round body in the nucleus, where synthesis of proteins takes place.
False 2: The chromatin is the dense round body in the nucleus, where synthesis of ribosomal subunits takes place.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The nucleus contains chromosomes, which are visible as rod-shaped structures only when the cell is about to divide.
False 1: The nucleus contains chromosomes, which are always visible as rod-shaped structures in non-dividing cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Chromosomes contain information for inheritance of characters from parents to the next generation in the form of DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) molecules; chromosomes are composed of DNA and specific proteins.
False 1: Chromosomes contain information for inheritance of characters in the form of RNA molecules.
False 2: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and carbohydrates.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The functional segments of DNA are called genes.
False 1: The functional segments of DNA are called chromosomes.
False 2: The functional segments of RNA are called genes.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In a non-dividing cell, DNA is present as part of chromatin material visible as an entangled mass of thread-like structures; whenever the cell is about to divide, the chromatin material gets organised into chromosomes.
False 1: In a non-dividing cell, DNA is present as organised chromosomes; whenever the cell is about to divide, chromosomes are converted back into chromatin material.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Mature Red Blood Cells (RBCs) in humans do not have a nucleus (enucleate); the absence of a nucleus provides more space for haemoglobin, allowing it to transport a larger amount of oxygen.
False 1: Mature Red Blood Cells (RBCs) in humans have a large nucleus, providing more space for haemoglobin.
False 2: Mature White Blood Cells (WBCs) in humans do not have a nucleus (enucleate), allowing them to transport more oxygen.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Since RBCs lack a nucleus, they cannot repair or divide themselves; as a result, they survive approximately for 120 days.
False 1: Since RBCs lack a nucleus, they cannot repair or divide themselves; as a result, they survive approximately for 12 days.
False 2: Since RBCs lack a nucleus, they cannot repair or divide themselves; as a result, they survive approximately for 1200 days.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In prokaryotic cells, DNA is present as a single circular molecule associated with specific proteins; the region containing this genetic material is called the nucleoid.
False 1: In prokaryotic cells, DNA is present as a single linear molecule.
False 2: The region containing genetic material in prokaryotic cells is called the nucleolus.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Ribosomes are tiny structures present either freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum; ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
False 1: Ribosomes are the sites of lipid synthesis.
False 2: Lysosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) is a large organelle that spreads like a network within the cytoplasm and is continuous with the outer membrane of the nuclear envelope.
False 1: The Golgi apparatus is a large organelle that spreads like a network within the cytoplasm and is continuous with the outer membrane of the nuclear envelope.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) has ribosomes attached to its surface and is mainly involved in protein synthesis and secretion; Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) lacks ribosomes and is involved in synthesis and storage of fats and hormones.
False 1: Rough ER lacks ribosomes and is involved in synthesis of fats and hormones; Smooth ER has ribosomes and is mainly involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
False 2: Smooth ER has ribosomes attached to its surface, making it look rough under an electron microscope.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The Golgi apparatus was first observed in 1898 by Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in the nerve cells of a barn owl.
False 1: The Golgi apparatus was first observed in 1898 by Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in the nerve cells of a frog.
False 2: The Golgi apparatus was first observed in 1889 by Italian scientist Camillo Golgi.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and/or lipids into vesicles for transport, secretion, or lysosome formation.
False 1: The endoplasmic reticulum modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and/or lipids into vesicles for transport, secretion, or lysosome formation.
False 2: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages carbohydrates into vesicles for transport.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Lysosomes are single membrane-bound sacs filled with enzymes which can break down unwanted proteins, carbohydrates, fats, and even damaged parts of the cell.
False 1: Vacuoles are single membrane-bound sacs filled with enzymes which can break down unwanted proteins, carbohydrates, and fats.
False 2: Lysosomes are double membrane-bound sacs filled with enzymes.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Mitochondria are often called the 'powerhouses of the cell' because they supply the energy needed for most cellular activities.
False 1: Chloroplasts are often called the 'powerhouses of the cell' because they supply the energy needed for most cellular activities.
False 2: Mitochondria are often called the 'protein factories of the cell' because they supply the energy needed for most cellular activities.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Each mitochondrion is surrounded by two membranes; the outer membrane is smooth and porous, while the inner membrane is folded into finger-like projections called cristae, which increase the surface area for chemical reactions and facilitate energy production.
False 1: The outer membrane of mitochondria is folded into finger-like projections called cristae; the inner membrane is smooth and porous.
False 2: The inner membrane of mitochondria is folded into projections called stroma, which increase the surface area for chemical reactions.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In mitochondria, glucose and other molecules are broken down to release energy during cellular respiration; the energy released is stored in the form of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate), which acts as the energy currency.
False 1: In chloroplasts, glucose and other molecules are broken down to release energy during cellular respiration.
False 2: In mitochondria, the energy released during cellular respiration is stored in the form of ADP.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Mitochondria and plastids have their own DNA and ribosomes, and can make some of their own proteins; these characteristics suggest both share an evolutionary history with single-celled organisms (bacteria).
False 1: Lysosomes and vacuoles have their own DNA and ribosomes, suggesting they share an evolutionary history with single-celled organisms.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Plants use special organelles called plastids for food synthesis and storage.
False 1: Plants use special organelles called mitochondria for food synthesis and storage.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: A green pigment called chlorophyll, present in the chloroplast, absorbs sunlight during photosynthesis.
False 1: A green pigment called chlorophyll, present in the mitochondria, absorbs sunlight during photosynthesis.
False 2: A yellow pigment called carotene, present in the chloroplast, absorbs sunlight during photosynthesis.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles; inside the chloroplast there is a semi-fluid substance called the stroma; within the stroma are disc-shaped membrane structures that contain chlorophyll.
False 1: Chloroplasts are single-membrane-bound organelles.
False 2: Inside the chloroplast there is a semi-fluid substance called the cristae.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In chromoplasts, plastids contain pigments other than chlorophyll (yellow, orange or red), which are the source of bright colours in flowers and fruits; these colours help attract pollinators and seed-dispersing animals.
False 1: In leucoplasts, plastids contain pigments other than chlorophyll (yellow, orange or red), which are the source of bright colours in flowers and fruits.
False 2: In chloroplasts, plastids contain pigments other than chlorophyll (yellow, orange or red), which are the source of bright colours in flowers and fruits.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food material such as starch, oils or proteins; for example, leucoplasts in potato and taro (Colocasia) cells store starch.
False 1: Chromoplasts are colourless plastids that store food material such as starch, oils or proteins.
False 2: Leucoplasts contain pigments such as yellow and orange carotenoids to give bright colours to fruits and flowers.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In a mature plant cell, there is usually one large central vacuole surrounded by a single selectively permeable membrane; the vacuole is filled with a watery fluid called cell sap.
False 1: In a mature animal cell, there is usually one large central vacuole surrounded by a single selectively permeable membrane.
False 2: In a mature plant cell, there are usually many small vacuoles distributed throughout the cytoplasm.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The vacuole stores water, minerals, sugars and waste material, and by storing large amounts of water, maintains pressure inside the cell, keeping the plant cell firm.
False 1: The mitochondrion stores water, minerals, sugars and waste material, and maintains pressure inside the plant cell.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: When a plant does not get enough water, the vacuole loses water, the cells become less firm, and the plant gets wilted.
False 1: When a plant does not get enough water, the vacuole gains water, the cells become more firm, and the plant stays upright.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In animal cells, vacuoles are sometimes present but are not as large as plant vacuoles; they help in the temporary storage of materials.
False 1: In animal cells, vacuoles are always present and are as large as plant vacuoles.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell; each new cell gets the same DNA and the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
False 1: Meiosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell.
False 2: Mitosis produces four genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Meiosis is a type of cell division that produces gametes and occurs only in the cells of reproductive organs.
False 1: Mitosis is a type of cell division that produces gametes and occurs only in the cells of reproductive organs.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In animals including humans, meiosis occurs only in the cells of testes of males to produce sperm and ovaries of females to produce eggs.
False 1: In animals including humans, mitosis occurs only in the cells of testes of males to produce sperm and ovaries of females to produce eggs.
False 2: In animals including humans, meiosis occurs in the testes of males to produce eggs and the ovaries of females to produce sperm.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In plants, meiosis occurs in the anthers (male parts) to form pollen grains and the ovaries (female parts) to produce egg cells.
False 1: In plants, meiosis occurs in the ovaries (female parts) to form pollen grains and the anthers (male parts) to produce egg cells.
False 2: In plants, mitosis occurs in the anthers to form pollen grains and the ovaries to produce egg cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In meiosis, the parent cell divides twice to form four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
False 1: In meiosis, the parent cell divides once to form two daughter cells with half the number of chromosomes.
False 2: In mitosis, the parent cell divides twice to form four daughter cells with half the number of chromosomes.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: During fertilisation, when gametes from two individuals combine, the original chromosome number is restored.
False 1: During fertilisation, when gametes from two individuals combine, the chromosome number is doubled beyond the original.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Errors in mitosis can lead to uncontrolled cell divisions, formation of tumours, and abnormal numbers of chromosomes in body cells.
False 1: Errors in meiosis lead to uncontrolled cell divisions and the formation of tumours.
False 2: Errors in mitosis lead to reduced cell divisions and a decreased number of chromosomes in body cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Errors in meiosis may result in genetic disorders associated with developmental problems or distinctive physical features; faulty meiosis may also cause early pregnancy loss or reduced fertility.
False 1: Errors in mitosis may result in genetic disorders associated with developmental problems or distinctive physical features.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In 1838, German botanist Matthias Schleiden reported that all plants are made up of cells.
False 1: In 1839, German botanist Matthias Schleiden reported that all plants are made up of cells.
False 2: In 1838, German zoologist Theodor Schwann reported that all plants are made up of cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In 1839, German zoologist Theodor Schwann found that all animals are also made up of cells.
False 1: In 1838, German zoologist Theodor Schwann found that all animals are also made up of cells.
False 2: In 1839, German botanist Matthias Schleiden found that all animals are also made up of cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In 1855, German scientist Rudolf Virchow expanded the Cell Theory by stating that new cells are formed only from pre-existing cells.
False 1: In 1855, German scientist Matthias Schleiden expanded the Cell Theory by stating that new cells are formed only from pre-existing cells.
False 2: In 1855, Rudolf Virchow stated that new cells are formed spontaneously from non-living matter.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: The classical Cell Theory states: all living organisms are made up of one or more cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; and all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
False 1: The classical Cell Theory states that all cells arise from spontaneous generation, not from pre-existing cells.
False 2: The classical Cell Theory states that the nucleus is the basic unit of structure and function in living beings.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In many animal cells, cell division usually stops when cells come in contact with neighbouring cells — a process called contact inhibition; cancer cells lose this control and keep dividing uncontrollably, leading to tumours.
False 1: In many plant cells, cell division stops when cells come in contact with neighbouring cells — a process called contact inhibition.
False 2: Cancer cells stop dividing when they come in contact with neighbouring cells, just like normal cells.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: Plant cells do not show contact inhibition due to their rigid cell walls and follow a different pattern of growth from animal cells.
False 1: Animal cells do not show contact inhibition due to their rigid cell walls.
False 2: Plant cells show contact inhibition due to their rigid cell walls.

Chapter: 9th New Ch02 - Cell: The Building Block of Life
True Statement: In 1902, Austrian botanist Gottlieb Haberlandt proposed that any living plant cell, even a fully mature cell from a permanent tissue, can develop into a complete plant if provided with suitable nutrients and favourable conditions — a property called totipotency.
False 1: In 1902, Austrian botanist Rudolf Virchow proposed that any living plant cell can develop into a complete plant — called totipotency.
False 2: In 1902, Gottlieb Haberlandt proposed that only undifferentiated (meristematic) plant cells can develop into a complete plant — called totipotency.
